sources.entry: Site Reliability Engineering for Native Mobile Apps - Abhijith Krishnappa - Case study: Halodoc adaptation of SRE principles for Native Mobile Apps

summary.name: Site Reliability Engineering for Native Mobile Apps
summary.one_liner: An InfoQ article by Halodoc's architect Abhijith Krishnappa describing how to apply Site Reliability Engineering principles, tools and team organization to native iOS and Android app development.
use_cases: Defining SLIs and SLOs for mobile app crashes and latency
Setting up phased rollouts and feature flags for mobile releases
Monitoring crashes and ANR issues in production apps
Organizing mobile teams with a platform team and stream-aligned teams
Running postmortems with RCA documents after app outages
Detecting memory leaks and security issues before release
summary.what_it_does: The article presents SRE tenets for mobile apps, including measuring reliability with SLIs, SLOs and SLAs, and tracking app availability through crashes and version management. It lists practices such as responding to Firebase Crashlytics velocity alerts, phased rollouts, feature flags, fuzz testing, and in-app updates. It covers performance monitoring with platform tools (Android Vitals, Xcode Instruments, Firebase Performance), debuggability through production logging, and monitoring tools like StrictMode, LeakCanary, Memgraph, MLeaksFinder and MobSF. The second half describes a three-phase organizational model in which a platform team enables stream-aligned teams to own SRE practices autonomously, with MTTR as the key metric.
notable: Describes Halodoc's in-house tools: NFMonitor, LiveConnect push mechanism, and Transporter production logging framework
Organization model moves from a platform team enabling stream-aligned teams to autonomous operation
Argues early-stage startups can adopt SRE sooner than is typical
caveats: Native mobile apps cannot be rolled back once released, which makes bugs harder to fix
Many of the described internal tools (NFMonitor, LiveConnect, Transporter) are Halodoc's in-house systems and are not available as public products
